title: St. Albert Home Rebates 2026: CEIP Is Full, With a $1,400 Incentive
desc: St. Albert home rebates for 2026: the City's CEIP offers up to $50,000 financing at 1.62% and a $1,400 incentive, but is at capacity. What else exists and what ended.
lead: St. Albert's CEIP is one of the cheapest sources of money in Alberta: up to $50,000 at 1.62% with a $1,400 incentive. It is at capacity and closed to pre-qualification right now. St. Albert has 25,940 households and the highest ownership rate of our Alberta cities.
cards_heading: What is open for St. Albert homes in 2026
cards_intro: We re-read each program page on October 3, 2026. Alberta has no provincial home rebates, so the help is local financing and a few small offers.

cards.title: St. Albert CEIP financing
cards.note: Financing up to 100% of project cost, repaid on the property tax bill over the lesser of 20 years or the upgrades' useful life. The rate is variable, and the program is at capacity with pre-qualification closed.

cards.title: CEIP incentive
cards.note: Applied to the Clean Energy Improvement Tax for each project, with a minimum project of $3,000.

cards.title: Utility rebates
cards.note: We found no primary source for a current ENMAX, ATCO, EPCOR or FortisAlberta heat pump or solar rebate, so we show none. Ask your utility before you buy.

cards.title: Federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability
cards.note: The federal program for oil-heated homes stopped taking Alberta applications after July 31, 2026.

cards.title: Canada Greener Homes Grant and Loan
cards.note: The grant's document deadline was December 31, 2025 and the loan cannot approve new applications.

cards.title: Greener Homes Affordability Program
cards.note: Alberta is not among the provinces taking part, as of August 31, 2026.

sections: 83% of St. Albert's 25,940 households own, and 70% live in detached houses. Only 1% live in buildings of five or more storeys. That makes a loan repaid on the property tax bill a good fit for most households, which is part of why the program fills up.

The City finances up to 100% of project cost, up to $50,000, repaid on the property tax bill over the lesser of 20 years or the upgrades' useful life. The rate is variable and was set at 1.62% with a maximum of 3% in the figures we read. The $1,400 incentive applies per project, and the project must be at least $3,000.

Pre-qualification is closed. People already in the queue are handled first come, first served. If you plan a project, ask the City when the next intake is expected and get quotes ready, because an incentive that is already spent does not come back.

About 35% of St. Albert's homes were built before 1981. The average January low is -14.4°C and the coldest day in our records reached -41.8°C. See our St. Albert heat pump page for what works in this climate.

The federal oil-to-heat-pump program stopped taking Alberta applications after July 31, 2026. The Greener Homes grant and loan are closed, and Alberta is not in the Greener Homes Affordability Program.
Questions to ask before you sign

If a contractor mentions the St. Albert CEIP, ask whether the project is already pre-qualified, because the City is not accepting new ones, and whether the quote assumes the $1,400 incentive. The incentive applies per project and the project must be at least $3,000, so a quote split into small pieces can lose it. A variable rate can also move, so ask what the maximum is.
claim_heading: What to do in St. Albert
claim_steps: Check the City's CEIP page for when pre-qualification reopens.
Get quotes of at least $3,000 so a project can qualify for the incentive.
Ask each quote to name any rebate it assumes.
Compare the CEIP rate with your own financing.
Keep invoices for any future program.
